properties.IncidentOverview: A storm moved through northern Harney County on July 22; 2026; yielding hundreds of positive lightning strikes. The Bald Mountain Fire was discovered on the afternoon of July 23; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone; Rangeland Fire Protection Association and the Egypt Fire responded promptly but were unable to contain the fast moving wildfire. Southern Area Team 2 is responsible for management of the fire; along with the Stubble; Crater; Second Flats and Jackass Butte fires. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

A lightning storm moved through Eastern Oregon on July 15; 2026; igniting multiple fires. The Egypt Fire was discovered on the morning of July 16; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone responded promptly but were spread thin due to several other starts in the area. Southern Area Team 2 took command of the Egypt Fire on July 19 at 6 AM. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

The New Pass fire is burning 30 miles northwest of Austin; Nevada; in grass and brush.

U.S. Wildland Fire Service wildland firefighters are responding to the Island Fire; which was reported on July 25 at approximately 9 p.m. The fire is located about 25 miles southwest of Ehrenberg; Arizona; in the Cibola National Wildlife Refuge. The fire is estimated to be approximately 3;145 acres and is 80% contained. Closures: The Cibola National Wildlife Refuge’s Island Management Unit is closed to the public and Hart Mine Road is closed at the refuge boundary. The bridge on Hart Mine Road crossing the Colorado River collapsed into the river. Pedestrians; motorists; and boaters should avoid the area.

An aggressive full-suppression strategy is in place for the Hat Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: The Fire remains within the current fire perimeter; with no movement. Yesterday; firefighters continued mopping up hotspots and extinguishing any burning or smoldering vegetation. The fire is 93 percent contained. Smoke may be visible from vegetation burning well within the perimeter of the fire area. Weather and Air Quality: The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Red Flag Warning for winds and low relative humidity; which is in effect from 3 PM MDT /2 PM PDT/ to 9 PM MDT /8 PM PDT/ Saturday. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies : Juntura RFPA; Owyhee County OEM; Idaho OEM; ODT; ODF; Idaho Power.

properties.Location: 25 Miles CW of Jordan Valley, OR
properties.IncidentOverview: An aggressive full-suppression strategy is in place for the Big Grass Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: Yesterday; the fire was very active on the east perimeter; especially in Boulder Creek; South Mountain; and Juniper Mountain areas due to hotter and drier conditions. Dozers; hand crews; and engines continued their aggressive action to construct and improve containment lines at the fire's edge. Their efforts were supported by water-dropping helicopters and air retardant drops; especially in steep and inaccessible areas. Today will be a critical fire weather day. The National Weather Service has issued a Red Flag Warning for gusty winds and low humidity; which could result in significant fire growth where line construction has not been completed. Firefighters will be working this morning to establish as much containment line as possible on the eastern perimeter before the wind event occurs this afternoon. Once the wind event begins; fire officials will prioritize firefighter safety and the protection of communities; structures; and critical infrastructure. Evacuations: The Owyhee County Sheriff has issued a Level 3 GO evacuation order for Triangle Reservoir; Pleasant Valley; South Mountain; Pleasant Valley Road to the City of Triangle; City of Triangle to the Triangle Reservoir; Flint Creek Road; Juniper Mountain Road; and the west portion of Mud Flat Road. A Level 2 SET status has been issued for Silver City . A Level 1 READY has been issued for the following zones: MAH-E063; MAH-E061; JOJ-E004; and JOJ-E003. Today; please monitor the Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office Facebook page for changing conditions and evacuation updates. BLM Area Closure: Access to the North Fork Campground along Juniper Mountain Road in Owyhee County is temporarily closed. The entire area south of Trout Creek Road and Silver City Road to the East Fork and Main Stem of the Owyhee River and from the Oregon border east to Highway 78 and Highway 51 is also temporarily closed. These closures are necessary to ensure the safety of both the public and firefighters involved in suppression efforts. Weather and Air Quality: The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Red Flag Warning for winds and low relative humidity; which is in effect from 3 PM MDT to 9 PM MDT Saturday. The winds and low humidity have the potential to significantly increase fire activity on the east side of the fire. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies: Jordan Valley RFPA; Owyhee RFPA; Malheur County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County OEM; Idaho OEM; ODT; Idaho Power; Idaho Department of Lands.

Ely; NV; August 1; 2026 — The WardFire; burning on Ward Mountain roughly 9 miles south of Ely; Nevada; is now estimated at 1;800 acres with 0% containment. The fire; first reported Friday morning; is burning in sagebrush; pinyon‑juniper; and mixed conifer fuels and is being managed under full suppression. Firefighters from the U.S. Forest Service; U.S. Wildland Fire Service; Nevada Division of Forestry; Ely Volunteer Fire Dept. and multiple contract resources made meaningful progress overnight; successfully holding portions of the fire along the lower eastern flank of Ward Mountain. However; extremely steep; rugged terrain continues to limit safe access for ground crews. Until a secure entry point can be established; firefighters are relying heavily on aircraft to slow the fire’s spread by building retardant lines and supporting future containment operations. Additional resources arrived overnight; increasing the total number of personnel assigned to the incident to more than 150 firefighters. The incident is currently supported by Engines (6); Dozers (4); Hand Crews including two Interagency Hotshot Crews (4); Water Tenders (2); Task Force (1); Helicopters including one Nevada National Guard helicopter (5); and a local Type 3 Incident Management Team has been stood up to oversee operations. No structures are currently threatened and there are currently no evacuation orders in place. White Pine County Sherriff’s Department will be the point of contact for evacuations; should the need arise. Public and firefighter safety remains the highest priority on the Incident. We thank the public for their cooperation and ongoing support in keeping away from the area; which helps firefighters concentrate on suppression efforts. No cause has been determined at this time. It remains under investigation. Updates will be available on the Humboldt‑Toiyabe NF Facebook page- https://www.facebook.com/HumboldtToiyabeNF and at NevadaFireInfo.org.
